true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check uses substring match

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, e.g. an origin `http://forum.example.co` passes when `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com/`. Impact is limited to iframe height manipulation, but the check should compare `e.origin` with the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post (stored XSS) `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the contents without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with `cook_method = raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim and it is rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and as `cooked` on the main site. The `url` comes from the user-controlled `embed_url` query parameter (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `import_remote`); only the host is validated, the path is attacker-controlled and URI parsing permits `'`. A URL such as `http:///x'onmouseover='alert(1)` breaks out of the href attribute and Nokogiri's `absolutize_urls` round-trip preserves the injected attribute. Escape `url` (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the anchor with Nokogiri.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is a malformed ERB block terminator

The header `if/else` block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. Ruby treats the trailing `if` as a statement modifier and, because a newline after `if` is permitted, consumes the next generated buffer-append statement as its condition. The template only works by accident (the append expression is truthy) and any change to the following markup can turn this into a syntax error or silently skip the `end`. It should be `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content.scrub` fails on RSS items and on Ruby < 2.1

SimpleRSS items only populate `content` for Atom feeds (RSS 2.0 items use `description`), so `i.content` is frequently `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the whole poll (the job also has `retry: false`). Additionally `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1; on the Ruby 2.0 this codebase targets it does not exist. Use `i.content || i.description` with a nil guard and avoid `scrub` or add a fallback. There is also no per-item rescue, so one bad item prevents importing all others.

false_positives.candidate:
Any unauthenticated visitor can create unlimited topics by varying embed_url

`EmbedController#best` enqueues `RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` that has no existing `TopicEmbed`. `TopicRetriever` only checks that the URL's host equals `embeddable_host` and throttles per exact URL (60s). An attacker who can set the Referer (or simply a visitor of the embedding site) can request `embed/best?embed_url=http://host/page?x=1`, `?x=2`, ... each of which passes the host check, triggers an outbound HTTP fetch of the page (plus a full RSS poll if enabled), and creates a brand new topic and post as `embed_by_username` because `import_remote` imports whatever 200 response comes back. This allows unbounded topic spam and outbound request amplification from unauthenticated requests. The URL should be normalized (strip query/fragment) and ideally only created when it appears in the feed or a per-host rate limit should be applied.

Failed PostCreator result treated as success

`PostCreator#create` returns the `Post` object even when creation was rolled back (e.g. host-spam detection), in which case the post is unsaved with errors. `post.present?` is true for such an object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` is attempted with `post_id: nil`/`topic_id: nil` and raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`, and `import` returns an unsaved post to callers. Check `post.errors.blank? && post.persisted?` instead.

Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to wrong absolute URLs

`absolutize_urls` treats every href/src starting with `/` as site-relative and strips all leading slashes, so a protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` becomes `http://<host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking images and links. Check for `start_with?('//')` and prefix only the scheme (or leave such URLs alone).

Success spec mocks TopicView.new with a nil return, so the best template cannot render

`TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` has no `returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil and `best.html.erb` calls `@topic_view.posts` on nil. The `after` hook asserts `response.should be_success`, so either this spec fails or the view is not actually being exercised. Return a stubbed topic view (with `posts` and `topic`) so the template, including the `end if` block and the header/footer branches, is genuinely rendered and verified.

import_remote relies on open-uri being loaded elsewhere

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on an http URL but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri`; the only `require 'open-uri'` is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. When autoloading (development, or any process where `Jobs::PollFeed` has not been referenced, e.g. `feed_polling_enabled` is false so `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` never touches it), `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so embeds are never retrieved. Add `require 'open-uri'` in `topic_embed.rb` (and preferably use an explicit HTTP client rather than `Kernel#open`, which also executes shell commands for strings beginning with `|`).

setnx/expire throttle is not atomic; key can become permanent

`retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx` and then a separate `$redis.expire`. If the process dies or the connection drops between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is left with no TTL and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff users, so the embed never loads. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or a MULTI block).

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
float: right on .small-action button is ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container

`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, which makes its direct children flex items. The CSS spec says `float` has no effect on flex items, so `button { float: right; }` (and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }`) no longer does anything. The action button (edit/delete on small-action posts) will now sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge, a visible layout regression. To keep the previous placement the button needs `margin-left: auto` (as was done for `.panel` in header.scss), and the dead `float` declarations should be removed.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin emits non-existent -ms-align-items and relies on value names that differ in legacy specs

`-ms-align-items` is not a property any version of IE ever implemented (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output. Additionally the legacy `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through unchanged, so any future call with `flex-start`/`flex-end` will silently produce invalid declarations for those engines. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, which happen to be shared, but the mixin as written is misleading.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin maps 0-based `order` directly onto 1-based -webkit-box-ordinal-group

`-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (2009 flexbox) is 1-based with a default of 1, while standard `order` is 0-based with a default of 0. Passing the same value to both means an element given `order(1)` would be placed at the same position as un-ordered siblings in legacy WebKit rather than after them. Current usages (2 and 3) happen to preserve relative ordering, but the mixin will produce inconsistent results across engines for other values; either offset the legacy value by 1 or drop the legacy prefix.

false_positives.candidate:
PR title/description do not describe the change; .valign-helper left as a now-meaningless flex item

The PR is titled as a header performance optimisation and the description is just "Test 5", but the change is actually a layout rewrite from floats to flexbox across header, topic, small-action posts and badges with visible behavioural differences. Reviewers and future readers of history cannot tell what was intended. Related leftover: `.valign-helper` (inline-block, height 100%, vertical-align middle) existed solely to vertically centre floated siblings; with `.contents` now using `align-items: center` it becomes an empty flex item and should be removed along with the markup that renders it.

The action button (edit/delete on small-action posts) will now sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge, a visible layout regression. true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder "refresh_token", which then overwrites the real refresh token in DB

When the refresh response lacks `refresh_token`, the function injects the string `"refresh_token"` into `data`. Callers spread this data over the stored credential (`o365AuthCredentials = {...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}` in office365calendar, `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` in zoomvideo), so the genuine refresh token is destroyed and replaced by a bogus string. Microsoft legitimately omits `refresh_token` on some refresh responses (the schema marks it optional), so this corrupts Office 365 credentials even with credential sync disabled, and permanently breaks the credential once the access token expires.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema is malformed; computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]" and all other fields are stripped

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]", so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown }`. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so when credential sync is enabled every parsed response only contains `access_token`; `expires_in`/`expiry_date` etc. are dropped. Callers then compute `Date.now() + undefined * 1000` (NaN expiry in Zoom) or lose the expiry entirely (Office365), causing the token to be considered expired/invalid on every call. The intent ('any numeric property is the expiry', 'allow other properties') cannot be expressed this way; use `.passthrough()` or an explicit schema.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object on every refresh

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. The previous code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the token object). Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` writes `{success, data}` into `credential.key`, so on the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for that user. This happens for every token refresh regardless of whether credential syncing is enabled, i.e. it corrupts all Google Calendar credentials in production.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. When syncing is enabled the helper returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, but several callers expect the shape of their own refresh client: hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` → NaN expiry, `accessToken` undefined), zohocrm and zoho-bigin expect an axios response (`tokenInfo.data` is undefined → TypeError), googlecalendar expects `{ res: { data } }` (`res?.data` undefined → TypeError). Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with no detail, and the surrounding `getToken` has no catch, so the failure propagates to callers (availability/booking) and debugging information about why MS rejected the refresh is gone.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` and no HTTP method restriction

The shared secret is checked with a plain string comparison, which leaks timing information and allows byte-by-byte guessing of the secret. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and does not guard against `req.headers[...]` being an array. Given this endpoint writes arbitrary third-party credentials for any user id, authentication should be hardened.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally; the new guard means a process detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`) is never killed, yet a replacement process for the same shards is started immediately. The still-running old process and the new one then both flush and produce the same shards concurrently, leading to duplicate segments on buffered-segments and leaked processes/Redis+Kafka connections on each restart (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index). The same false check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called there. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying bug: spawn-context processes are SpawnProcess instances that fail the multiprocessing.Process isinstance check on POSIX, preventing hung flusher processes from being killed.
